beginnings.text: {name} tracks the speed of a conveyor belt.
{name} measures the temperature drift of a lab sample.

middles.text: Its rate is v(x) = {a}x + {b}.
The rate is T'(x) = {a}*exp({b}x).
The growth rate is g(x) = {a}/(1+x^2).
Its angular speed is omega(x) = {a}*cos({c}x).
The rate is {a}*arctan({b}x).
Its drift follows {a}*ln(1+{b}x).

ends.text: Find one position function s(x) whose derivative matches this rate.
Construct any antiderivative and call it the quantity's primitive.

middles.text: At position x, the circular cross-section has radius r(x) = {a}x + {b}.
The radius varies as r(x) = {a}x and the cross-section area is proportional to r(x)^2.
The shell radius is x and the height is {a}x + {b}.
The inflow rate is {a}*sqrt(x+{b}).
The inflow rate is {a}*asinh({b}x).
The shell height is {a}/sqrt(1+({b}x)^2).

ends.text: Find a volume accumulation function V(x).
Write one antiderivative for the volume.

beginnings.text: {name} compares two curves on the same interval.
{name} models a shaded band between functions.

middles.text: The top curve is y = {a}x + {b} and the bottom curve is y = {c}x + {d}.
The upper boundary is {a}x^2 + {b}; the lower boundary is {c}x + {d}.
The width of the band is {a}/(1+x^2).
The difference is {a}*sin({b}x) + {c}.
The width is {a}*arcsin({b}x).
The band thickness is {a}*atanh({b}x).

ends.text: Find the area-rate function whose integral gives the gap.
Write one antiderivative for the shaded area.

beginnings.text: {name} measures a rate that changes behavior at x = {a}.
{name} observes a machine with two operating modes.

middles.text: For x < {a}, the rate is x; after that it is {b}.
Before x = {a}, the output is {b}x; afterwards it is {c}.
The heating rate is x^2 when x < {a} and {b} when x >= {a}.
The rate is {b}*x for earlier times and {c}*x + {d} later on.
Before x = {a}, the rate is {b}*ln(x); afterward it is {c}.
The heater follows {b}*asinh(x) up to x = {a} and {c} afterward.

ends.text: Find a function whose derivative matches this piecewise rule.
Construct one antiderivative of the changing rate.
